claims.text: What the strip looks like ST elevation with later Q waves in the precordial leads (V1–6), ± the high lateral leads, often preceded by hyperacute T waves.
claims.quote: ST segment elevation with subsequent Q wave formation in precordial leads (V1-6) +/- high lateral leads. These changes are often preceded by hyperacute T waves

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) ST elevation: V1–V4; reciprocal ST depression in II, III, aVF; likely artery LAD (anteroseptal, V1–V2: proximal LAD)
claims.quote: Location ST Elevation Reciprocal ST Depression Likely Artery Anterior V1–V4 II, III, aVF LAD Anteroseptal V1–V2 — LAD (proximal)

claims.text: Reciprocal change: mainly III and aVF; its size follows the ST elevation in I and aVL, so it may be minimal or absent when the high lateral leads aren't involved
claims.quote: Reciprocal ST depression in inferior leads (mainly III and aVF) NB: The magnitude of reciprocal change in inferior leads is determined by the magnitude of ST elevation in I and aVL (as these leads are electrically opposite III and aVF), and hence may be minimal or absent in anterior STEMIs that do not involve high lateral leads.

claims.text: Named by maximal ST elevation: septal V1–2; anterior V2–5; anteroseptal V1–4; anterolateral V3–6 + I, aVL; extensive anterior V1–6 + I, aVL
claims.quote: The different infarct patterns are named according to the leads with maximal ST elevation: Septal = V1-2 Anterior = V2-5 Anteroseptal = V1-4 Anterolateral = V3-6, I + aVL Extensive anterior / anterolateral = V1-6, I + aVL

claims.text: ECG pattern and actual infarct location often correlate poorly
claims.quote: there is often a poor correlation between ECG features and precise infarct location as determined by imaging or autopsy

claims.text: Wraparound LAD: ST elevation in the precordial and inferior leads at once
claims.quote: Anterior-inferior STEMI due to occlusion of a “wraparound” LAD. This presents with simultaneous ST elevation in the precordial and inferior leads

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Artery: usually LAD occlusion
claims.quote: Anterior STEMI usually results from occlusion of the left anterior descending artery (LAD).
claims.locator: Clinical Relevance of Anterior Myocardial Infarction

claims.text: Proximal LAD or left main occlusion has a much worse prognosis — a larger territory and worse hemodynamics
claims.quote: Proximal LAD / LMCA occlusion has a significantly worse prognosis due to larger infarct territory size and more severe haemodynamic disturbance
claims.locator: Prediction of the Site of LAD Occlusion

claims.text: Significance The poorest prognosis of all infarct locations, from the larger area of myocardium
claims.quote: Anterior myocardial infarction carries the poorest prognosis of all infarct locations, due to the larger area of myocardium infarct size.
claims.locator: Clinical Relevance of Anterior Myocardial Infarction

claims.text: One study, anterior vs inferior MI: in-hospital mortality 11.9 vs 2.8%, total mortality 27 vs 11%, heart failure 41 vs 15%
claims.quote: A study comparing outcomes from anterior and inferior infarctions (STEMI + NSTEMI) found that compared with inferior MI, patients with anterior MI had higher incidences of: In-hospital mortality (11.9 vs 2.8%) Total mortality (27 vs 11%) Heart failure (41 vs 15%)
claims.locator: Clinical Relevance of Anterior Myocardial Infarction

claims.text: Treatment As for STEMI: emergency PCI is preferred when it can be done in time (door-to-balloon < 90 minutes, < 120 with transfer) by an experienced operator
claims.quote: For patients with STEMI, emergency PCI is the preferred treatment of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction when available in a timely fashion (door to balloon-inflation time < 90 minutes, or < 120 minutes if hospital-to-hospital transfer is involved) by an experienced operator

notes.issue: claim dropped the quote's condition (timely, experienced operator)
notes.resolution: claim now says PCI is preferred when it can be done in time by an experienced operator; re-checked pass
